title: Jangoo, Chase’s defiant stand takes WI close to parity
summary: Amir Jangoo may not have even featured in the opening Test for West Indies had Shai Hope not suffered an injury during training. But with a chance handed out, he made full use of it to rescue the hosts from a precarious position to leave them only 37 behind Sri Lanka’s first-innings 308. Jangoo, playing his second Test, walked in at 97 for 2 in the afternoon, and showed off an obdurate batting style, taking 174 balls for his unbeaten 78. His maiden Test half-century took West Indies to 271 for 5 at stumps. At the other end, a man with something else to prove batted on from No. 7 – Roston Chase, the West Indies captain who has averaged 15.50 in the 15 innings he has batted since July 2025. Watchful in dead-batting and playing the long game, he joined Jangoo in the middle at 168 for 5, took 105 balls to score 42, and contributed to an unbeaten sixth-wicket partnership of 103 to leave the hosts the happier side after day two. Their stand was crucial because it came after a middle-session where West Indies lost 4 for 79, losing the gains they had achieved in the morning session, with the openers helping them reach 89 for 1 at lunch. John Campbell (39) and Brandon King (31) saw off the new ball and enjoyed a half-century stand in the morning. The runs came West Indies’ way right from the start of the day when Lahiru Kumara sprayed the ball wide in his only over of the session, conceding two four-byes, before leaving the field for the rest of the day with a hamstring niggle. Asitha Fernando and Kasun Rajitha operated close to the corridor of uncertainty but the openers saw them out successfully against the new ball. Boundaries from Campbell and King came the classical way – on-drives past the non-striker or crisp shots square on either side – but the occasional mistimed slash also found the fence. title: Heartbreak for Scotland as SL clinch thriller to stay alive
summary: Sri Lanka kept their faint chances of reaching the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup alive with a nervy victory over Scotland in Manchester. Chasing 152, they required seven runs from the final over. Nilakshika Silva and Sugandika Kumari managed four off the first three balls from Rachel Slater before the seamer left the field with a knee injury. Priyanaz Chatterji was called upon to finish the over, conceding a single before Kumari slashed through short third for a decisive boundary with two balls to spare. Sri Lanka now depend on England beating New Zealand and Ireland inflicting a heavy defeat on West Indies to reach the final four. Scotland, meanwhile, missed a golden chance to secure direct qualification for the 2028 edition. Darcey Carter and Katherine Fraser gave Scotland early momentum. Carter attacked from the outset, striking four boundaries in her first ten balls, while Fraser added two more before falling to a sharp catch by Silva at mid-off. Carter, who became the tournament’s leading run-scorer during the powerplay, guided Scotland to 45 for 1 alongside captain Kathryn Bryce. Sri Lanka regained control after the fielding restrictions eased. Bryce briefly countered with a six and a four off Chamari Athapaththu but was dismissed for 23 by Kavisha Dilhari. Carter, after a brisk start, struggled to find gaps and managed only 34 from 36 balls. Scotland’s scoring slowed to just 43 runs in the eight overs following the powerplay. Ailsa Lister and Sarah Bryce revived the innings with a 53-run stand in 32 balls. Lister was run out for 26, followed immediately by Chatterji, but Sarah Bryce pressed on, striking two boundaries in the final over to push Scotland past 150. Their late surge added 63 runs in the last six overs. title: WI wrap SL up for 308 despite Dhananjaya 120
summary: Dhananjaya de Silva’s commanding 120 off 168 deliveries was the backbone of Sri Lanka’s resistance on day one of the Test series against West Indies. His innings, full of authority and flair, helped the hosts recover from a shaky start after losing three wickets in the opening hour. Kemar Roach struck in the first over, before Alzarri Joseph removed two batters in three balls during the 10th over to leave Sri Lanka reeling at 42 for 3. On a surface offering assistance to the quicks, Sri Lanka clawed back through Dinesh Chandimal’s counterattacking half-century, followed by de Silva’s assured strokeplay across the middle and evening sessions. De Silva’s knock was built on three crucial partnerships: 68 with Chandimal, 99 with Sonal Dinusha, and 64 with Milan Rathnayaka. Dinusha’s restrained 43 off 75 balls provided valuable support, while Rathnayaka’s 27 ensured Sri Lanka crossed the 300 mark. Sri Lanka’s total of 308 was competitive rather than commanding. West Indies’ seamers — Roach, Alzarri, and Shamar Joseph — were consistently threatening, but it was Justin Greaves’ medium pace that proved decisive. He dismissed de Silva midway through the final session and added two tail-end scalps to finish with 3 for 39. Roach, Alzarri, and Shamar claimed two wickets apiece. West Indies faced one over before stumps and survived unscathed, though their over rate was sluggish, with only 72.5 overs bowled across six-and-a-half hours. De Silva’s innings sparkled with disdainful pulls and crisp drives. He repeatedly punished Alzarri Joseph, spanking him through point and then pulling him through square leg in the same over. Though frequently beaten on the outside edge, he kept the scoreboard ticking with singles and twos, while scoring heavily through cover and deep third. Dinusha, meanwhile, capitalized on short, wide deliveries, particularly through backward point. title: Athapaththu’s Record Blitz Powers Sri Lanka Women to Nine‑Wicket Win
summary: Skipper Chamari Athapaththu lit up Bristol with a blistering unbeaten 106 off just 61 deliveries, decorated with 17 fours and two sixes, as Sri Lanka Women cruised to a commanding nine‑wicket victory over Ireland Women in their T20 World Cup fixture today. This innings also marked herfourth T20I century, underlining her status as one of the most destructive batters in women’s cricket. Ireland Women were restricted to 130 for 5, with Gaby Lewis top‑scoring with 59 and Alice Tector adding 28. Sri Lanka chased down the target in only 15.3 overs, losing just one wicket, thanks to Athapaththu’s special innings. Imesha Dulani provided solid support with 20 runs. Scores: Ireland Women: 130/5 (20.0 ) (Gaby Lewis 59, Alice Tector 28) Sri Lanka Women: 134/1 (15.3 ) ( Chamari Athapaththu 106* , Imesha Dulani 20)

title: Tharanga Dominates Doha with 88.68m Monster Throw
summary: Sri Lankan star Rumesh Tharanga captured another remarkable victory at the Doha Diamond League, launching a monster throw of 88.68m to defeat a world-class field that featured Olympic and World Champions , including his idol, Neeraj Chopra. At just 23 years old, the current world leader entered Doha after back-to-back wins in Rome and Ostrava. Initially struggling in fourth place after his first three attempts, Tharanga unleashed a massive 88.68m throw on his fourth try, sealing the win ahead of double World Champion Anderson Peters of Grenada (86.38m), Curtis Thompson of the USA (85.99m), and India’s 2021 Olympic Champion Neeraj Chopra (85.69m). Earlier this month, Tharanga made global headlines with a record-breaking 92.62m throw in Rome , the first throw beyond 92m in two years  instantly becoming an overnight sensation. He now sits second in the world rankings, the highest ever position achieved by a Sri Lankan athlete, and carries the reputation as the man to beat in javelin. He also leads the Diamond League standings in the discipline, with a second place finish in Rabat followed by emphatic wins in Rome and Doha. A former Peterite trained under coach Tony Prasanna, Tharanga now owns all five of the best throws recorded in 2026. His achievements have propelled him to eighth place on the all-time list of javelin throwers , a remarkable feat for the rising star.

title: Rumesh Tharanga Climbs to World No. 2 After Ostrava Triumph
summary: Following another monster throw in Ostrava yesterday, Sri Lanka’s javelin sensation Rumesh Tharanga Pathiragae has climbed to second place in the World Athletics rankings, moving up from third. Germany’s Julian Weber continues to lead with 1360 points, while Tharanga now sits close behind on 1333 points. In 2026, Tharanga has been nothing short of dominant, registering all of the top four throws of the year — an unprecedented achievement for a Sri Lankan athlete in any discipline. The 23‑year‑old, trained under Tony Prasanna, continued his golden run in Europe by clinching gold at the Ostrava Golden Spike competition in the Czech Republic with a throw of 86.57m. Competing in this World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event, he opened with 85.87m, improved to 86.30m on his second attempt, and sealed victory with 86.57m on his third. That effort was more than enough to secure the top spot. Double World Champion Anderson Peters of Grenada finished second with 84.27m, while South Africa’s Douw Smit claimed third with 83.90m. Earlier this month in Rome, Tharanga stunned the athletics world with a throw of 92.62m, making him the 8th best thrower of all time. In Ostrava, unlike Rome, he entered as the clear favorite  the “man to beat” in world javelin this year. He was even featured as the face of the competition during the pre‑event press conference alongside US Olympic pole vault champion Katie Moon. Currently ranked second in the world, Tharanga owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5th best throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new era of dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following Ostrava, Tharanga will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning home. Next month, he is set to represent Sri Lanka at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland, where expectations will be sky‑high.

title: Ananda Ends 23-Year Wait with Historic Victory Over St. Thomas’ College
summary: Ananda College Rugby produced one of the most memorable moments in the school’s sporting history by defeating St. Thomas’ College and ending a 23-year wait for victory over the Mount Lavinia outfit in the Schools Rugby League encounter played at Rajagiriya. The landmark triumph is more than just a win. It is the latest chapter in a remarkable resurgence that has transformed Ananda into one of the most courageous and competitive teams in Division ‘A’ rugby this season. Having returned to the top division after a lengthy absence, many observers expected Ananda to struggle against the established powerhouses. Instead, the Maroon and Gold warriors have earned admiration across the rugby fraternity for their fearless approach, commitment, and fighting spirit. Week after week, they have challenged stronger and more experienced opponents, refusing to be intimidated by reputation or history. This victory over St. Thomas’ is a fitting reward for a team that has consistently punched above its weight throughout the season. While the league table may not fully reflect their performances, several narrow defeats in the opening weeks denied Ananda the opportunity of securing a place in the Cup Segment. Those close losses, often decided by the finest of margins, masked the true quality of this young side. Many rugby followers would agree that based on performances alone, Ananda deserved to be among the Cup Segment contenders. The team’s ability to compete with the best schools in the country, despite being newcomers to Division ‘A’, has been one of the stories of the 2026 season. The victory against St. Thomas’ also underlines the remarkable progress achieved by the coaching staff, management, players, and supporters who have worked tirelessly to rebuild the rugby programme. What has stood out most is the character of the players. Time and again they have shown resilience, determination, and an unwavering belief in their ability to compete at the highest level. title: Shanaka, Mishara fifties set up series-levelling win for Sri Lanka
summary: Dasun Shanaka produced the batting ballistics, Kamil Mishara held the innings together, and Sri Lanka’s spinners dominated the middle overs, comfortably defending their 194 for 6. This 37-run victory brings Sri Lanka level 1-1 in the series against West Indies, with one match to play on Sunday night. Sri Lanka had been struggling at 88 for 4 in the 13th over when Shanaka joined Mishara at the crease. The pair then blasted 103 off 42 balls together to propel Sri Lanka to a commanding score of 194 for 6, hitting seven sixes and nine fours between them. Although Sri Lanka struck twice with the new ball, West Indies had still looked confident in pursuit at 89 for 2, until Sri Lanka’s spinners went to work. A run out would spark a collapse that cost West Indies six wickets for 32 runs. They struggled to recover from 122 for 8 after 15 overs. Dushmantha Chameera, who had struck early in the innings and was effective in the other phases as well, closed out the match in the 19th over, taking three wickets for 9 runs. West Indies were 157 all out, despite Rovman Powell and Shimron Hetmyer having put on 81 off 47 for the third wicket. Although he arrived at the crease with Sri Lanka in some trouble, Shanaka was almost immediately aggressive, blasting Roston Chase’s offspin onto the roof of the Sabina Park stadium fourth ball, before crashing him for a four and thumping another six next ball. All three of these boundaries came through deep midwicket. He also struck a huge six down the ground, and hooked a ball over fine leg as well, as he stormed to a 19-ball fifty. title: Rumesh to Compete in Ostrava on Tuesday
summary: By Anjana Kaluarachchi After his heroic performance in Rome that made world headlines, javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga will head to the Czech Republic to compete in the Golden Ostrava on Tuesday, 16 June, a World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event. Tharanga, who threw 92.62m to become the 8thbest thrower of all time, will once again face double world champion Anderson Peters of Grenada and former Olympic gold medalist Thomas Röhler of Germany, among other top competitors. Unlike in Rome, Rumesh will enter the competition as the favorite, carrying the tag of ‘man to beat’ in world javelin this year. The 23-year-old former Peterite is currently ranked third in the world and owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5thbest throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new level of world dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following his heroic performance in Rome, Tharanga stayed in Italy for a week, training in both Rome and Milan, before departing for the Czech Republic yesterday. description: By Anjana Kaluarachchi After his heroic performance in Rome that made world headlines, javelin thrower Rumesh Tharanga will head to the Czech Republic to compete in the Golden Ostrava on Tuesday, 16 June, a World Athletics Continental Tour Gold event. Tharanga, who threw 92.62m to become the 8thbest thrower of all time, will once again face double world champion Anderson Peters of Grenada and former Olympic gold medalist Thomas Röhler of Germany, among other top competitors. Unlike in Rome, Rumesh will enter the competition as the favorite, carrying the tag of ‘man to beat’ in world javelin this year. The 23-year-old former Peterite is currently ranked third in the world and owns the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 5thbest throws of the season. He is the first Sri Lankan athlete in history to achieve such a high global ranking in a specific event, marking a new level of world dominance for Sri Lankan athletics. Following his heroic performance in Rome, Tharanga stayed in Italy for a week, training in both Rome and Milan, before departing for the Czech Republic yesterday. Following Ostrava, Tharanga will compete in the Diamond League in Doha before returning to Sri Lanka. Next month, he will head to Scotland to represent the country at the Commonwealth Games.
